rows.description: A teenager after a breakup or friend group split may withdraw, post cryptic messages or throw themselves into activity. Heartbreak can feel overwhelming, and support from friends and family helps recovery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, detachment, overwhelm

rows.description: A teenager notices a friend who is quiet, tired or joking less and wonders about their state. A gentle question such as how are you really is better than guessing, and serious worry goes to a trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, anxiety, curiosity, tiredness

rows.description: A teenager recognises an eye-roll, curled lip or dismissive tone that says you are beneath me. Contempt is hurtful and damages trust, so the wise response is to name the effect calmly or leave.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: contempt, calm, trust, hurt

rows.subtype: Defiant, irritated and frustrated with authority [Mismatch]
rows.description: A teenager's sullen silence, backtalk or refusal may mean anger, fear, wish for autonomy or exhaustion. Adults who ask before punishing learn more and keep communication open.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, hostility, fear, tiredness

rows.description: A teenager with intense rage may shout, slam doors or go silent and cold. Fury peaks and fades, so stepping away, breathing and returning later to talk protects relationships.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, relief from stress

rows.description: A teenager notices a peer glaring, sneering or blocking the way and feels unsafe. Hostility is a warning to disengage, stay near others and involve a trusted adult, not to retaliate.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hostility, interest, trust

rows.subtype: Apologetic and pleading in peer conflict [Interpreting]
rows.description: A teenager reads a friend's quick sorry, soft voice or begging texts and wonders if they are sincere. Sincerity shows in changed behaviour over time, and pressure to forgive should not override boundaries.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: curiosity, awe

rows.description: A teenager may feel I did something bad or I am bad, and the two look alike from outside. Guilt motivates repair, while shame drives hiding, so adults respond to the person with care.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: shame, guilt

rows.description: A teenager blushes, avoids the spotlight or overthinks how they seem. Self-consciousness peaks in these years, and small steps into social situations build comfort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager nodding while glancing at a phone may be listening or elsewhere. Attention cannot be read from posture alone, so asking a brief question checks it.
